title: PvP: defender evasion is a flat, uncounterable dodge — DEX never answers it in a duel (live path diverges from the tuned sim)
claim: In duels the whole DEX-vs-EVA tier system (Stats.dex_tier / graze_through) is bypassed. `_hit_rival` deliberately resolves against NEUTRAL defenses (e_eva = 0), so no dex/eva interaction happens attacker-side; the strike then crosses the wire and lands on the owner via `p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, ...)` with attacker == null, which takes the attacker-less branch and rolls a bare `randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva)`. The striker's DEX is never consulted on either side — it is not even carried on the wire (pvp_strike ships only `pen`). So a duel evasion stack is an uncounterable ~50-65% dodge, contradicting eva_curve's own contract ("answerable by ~matching dex") and, more concretely, the balance harness the PvP numbers were tuned on: pvp_duel_sim._hit DOES model the tier (miss / graze / cancel). Live behaviour and the simulator disagree.
evidence:
player_combat.gd:1898-1899 `	var result := Stats.resolve(base_amt * (1.0 - true_frac), dmg_type,
		crit, crit_dmg, 0.0, dex, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, crit_exempt)`  (e_eva argument is 0.0 -> resolve's dex_tier block is a no-op)
net/net_session.gd:3053 `			p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, false, pen)`  (attacker == null)
player.gd:1120-1125 `	else:
		if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):
			game.spawn_text(global_position + Vector2(0, -40), "DODGE!", Color(0.7, 0.9, 1.0))
			game.sfx("blink")
			_uniq_on_evade(attacker)
			return`
tests/pvp_duel_sim.gd:506-512 `		var tier := Stats.dex_tier(f_dex, e_eva)
		if tier < 2 and randf() < float(o["eva"]):
			if tier == 0:
				return          # full miss
			grazed = true       # graze — leaks the curve's fraction through
			graze_frac = Stats.graze_through(f_dex, e_eva)`
repro: Duel an assassin/archer that has stacked Jade (eva) gems, e.g. eva = 0.60 raw -> Stats.eva_curve = 0.50 + 0.10*EVA_OVERCAP_RATE(0.06) = 0.506. Attacker equips Amber (dex) gems to any value — 0, 200, 2000. Every strike still resolves attacker-side with e_eva = 0.0 (never a miss, never a graze), then the owner rolls a flat 50.6% dodge with no dex input. Expected per pvp_duel_sim and the Stats.dex_tier contract: at dex >= eff_eva / DEX_PER_EVA (parity) the dodge is cancelled outright (tier 2) and 100% of strikes land. Actual: ~half the strikes are voided regardless of DEX, and Amber gems buy zero offensive answer in PvP.
fix: Carry the striker's DEX over the same seam that already carries pen: add a `dex` parameter to net_session.pvp_strike / _rpc_pvp_strike / _pvp_apply_strike (bounded with `_fin` beside the existing `pen = _fin(pen, 1.0e6, 0.0)`), pass `dex` from player_combat._hit_rival's `game.net_session().pvp_strike(...)` call, and thread it into `Player.take_damage(..., pvp_pen, pvp_dex)`. In the attacker-less branch of player.gd:1120 use the same tier logic the attacker branch gets — `var tier := Stats.dex_tier(pvp_dex, eff_eva)` and `Stats.graze_through` for the tier-1 clip — so hazards/telegraphs (pvp_dex 0.0) keep exactly today's behaviour while a duel strike is answered by DEX. No new tuning numbers are needed (DEX_PER_EVA / DEX_GRAZE_RATIO / GRAZE_CURVE_EXP already live in balance.gd).

title: TRUE damage can be fully dodged on the attacker-less path (poison pools, telegraphs, true-typed duel strikes)
claim: stats.gd's contract is explicit — "true" (ignores all defenses, cannot crit) — and Stats.resolve gates BOTH the evasion roll and the crit roll behind `if dmg_type != "true"` ("True damage always hits"). The attacker-less branch of Player.take_damage rolls evasion BEFORE it checks the damage type: the `dmg_type != "true"` guard sits on the resistance line (1126) and on the Mirrorstep cut (1131), but not on the dodge roll at 1121. Every attacker-less true-damage source is therefore dodgeable by an evasion build, at up to ~65% (CAP_EVA plus EVA_OVERCAP_RATE overflow).
evidence:
player.gd:1120-1131 `	else:
		if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):
			...
			return
		if dmg_type != "true":
			...
			amount *= (1.0 - Stats.res_frac(maxf(0.0, res - pvp_pen)))
		if dash_guard_time > 0.0 and dmg_type != "true":`
stats.gd:106-116 `		# DEX answers evasion as a TIER (dex_tier) ... True damage always hits.
		var grazed := false
		if dmg_type != "true":
			var tier := dex_tier(dex, e_eva)`
game_flow.gd:2221-2222 `				"poison":
					lp.take_damage(6.0, "true")`
repro: Stand a hero with Jade gems (eva raw 0.50 -> eva_curve 0.50) inside a poison hazard pool (game_flow.gd:2222 ticks `take_damage(6.0, "true", attacker=null)`). Expected: 6 damage every tick, no dodge — the pool is true damage. Actual: ~half the ticks print "DODGE!" and deal 0, so the pool's DPS is halved for that build. Same path fires for a true-typed PvP strike (assassin `quietus` sets effects["type"]="true" below the HP threshold; net_session.gd:3053 lands it with attacker == null), where a dodged true hit contradicts the item card outright.
fix: Move the type guard onto the roll: `if dmg_type != "true" and randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):` at player.gd:1121. That matches Stats.resolve's own ordering and leaves the attacker-present branch (which already delegates the guard to resolve) untouched. No tuning numbers involved.

title: PvP brittle stacks past the balance cap and never decay (+32% permanent vs PvE's +20% for 6s)
claim: The rival-shell brittle counter hardcodes a cap of 8 instead of Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS (5), and — unlike every other rider parked on the shell — it has no decay clock. pvp.gd's `_tick_rival_riders` ages vuln_time, slow_time, stun_time, crush_t, res_shred_t, burn_time and bleed_time, but there is no `brittle_t` on the shell and nothing decrements `brittle`; it is only zeroed at a round boundary. `_hit_rival` multiplies with the SAME `Balance.BRITTLE_PER_STACK` the PvE path uses, so the ice line's synergy amp is 8 * 0.04 = +32% and permanent for the round, where the enemy path caps at 5 * 0.04 = +20% and expires after BRITTLE_DUR (6.0s).
evidence:
player_core.gd:642-645 `func add_brittle() -> void:
	if not _rival_shell():
		return
	brittle = mini(brittle + 1, 8)`
enemy.gd:2328-2331 `func add_brittle() -> void:
	_mirror_status("brittle", {})
	brittle = mini(brittle + 1, Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS)
	brittle_t = Balance.BRITTLE_DUR`
enemy.gd:875-877 `	brittle_t = maxf(0.0, brittle_t - delta)
	if brittle_t <= 0.0:
		brittle = 0`
pvp.gd:99-105 `	foe.vuln_time = maxf(0.0, foe.vuln_time - delta)
	foe.slow_time = maxf(0.0, foe.slow_time - delta)
	foe.stun_time = maxf(0.0, foe.stun_time - delta)
	foe.crush_t = maxf(0.0, foe.crush_t - delta)
	foe.res_shred_t = maxf(0.0, foe.res_shred_t - delta)
	if foe.res_shred_t <= 0.0:
		foe.res_shred = 0.0`  (no brittle line)
player_combat.gd:1945-1947 `	if effects.get("brittle", 0):
		dmg *= 1.0 + q.brittle * Balance.BRITTLE_PER_STACK
		q.add_brittle()`
balance.gd:1587-1589 `const BRITTLE_PER_STACK := 0.04
const BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS := 5
const BRITTLE_DUR := 6.0`
repro: Ice-themed mage duels anyone. Land 8 brittle-tagged hits (Frost Nova / ice a1) anywhere in the round, then stop for 30 seconds and hit again. Expected (PvE parity): stacks capped at 5 and gone 6s after the last application, so the late hit takes +0%. Actual: q.brittle sits at 8 for the whole round, so every subsequent hit — including the one 30s later — is multiplied by 1.32.
fix: Two one-line changes, both toward the existing knobs. (1) player_core.gd:645 -> `brittle = mini(brittle + 1, Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS)` (removes the bare 8; the tuning number already lives in balance.gd). (2) Give the shell a `var brittle_t := 0.0` next to `var brittle := 0` (player_core.gd:586), stamp it `brittle_t = Balance.BRITTLE_DUR` in add_brittle, and age it in pvp.gd `_tick_rival_riders` in the shape res_shred already uses: `foe.brittle_t = maxf(0.0, foe.brittle_t - delta)` / `if foe.brittle_t <= 0.0: foe.brittle = 0`. `_clear_rival_riders` should zero `brittle_t` alongside `brittle`.

title: Band variant authored before the "already talked" flag variant makes six NPC greetings repeatable resonance/gold faucets
claim: `_convo_variant` returns the FIRST matching variant and evaluates each entry's `band` before its `flag` in authored order. Six greeting nodes list a `band` variant BEFORE the `<npc>_met` flag variant that carries the `"next"` short-circuit. For a player standing in that band the band variant always wins, the short-circuit never fires, and the node re-presents its full, ungated choice list on every re-talk — so the choice's resonance shift AND `_resonance_reward`'s gold drop are paid again each time. Two of the six are unbounded because the choice keeps the player inside the shadowing band.
repro: Chapter 2, resonance >= 25 (steady band, Story.RES_BAND_AT = 25.0 at story.gd:9). Walk up to The Tracker in a social room and press E: variant 1 (`band: steady`) matches, it has no `"next"`, so `force_linear` is false (game_base.gd:1995) and both choices show. Pick "What does the edge do…": +3.0 resonance and 14 gold drop. Walk away, press E again — `ch2_tracker_met` is set but the steady variant still matches first, so the same two choices reappear. Repeat: resonance clamps at +100 (player_core.gd:49) but `res_delta != 0.0` stays true, so the 14-gold drop is an unlimited faucet. Identical loop on Gentle Suli in ch5 for 16 gold a cycle. Correct behaviour (neutral/tempted band on the tracker): the second talk ends immediately on the `ch2_tracker_met` line.
fix: Content-side, one line moved per node — reorder the variants so each progress/`_met` flag variant sits ABOVE the `band` variant, matching the house pattern at ch4_zones.gd:275-277: in ch2_zones_side.gd swap 266<->267 and 224<->225, in ch4_zones.gd swap 417<->418, in ch5_zones.gd swap 354<->355, in promises_kept.gd move line 111 above 110, in promises_kept_2.gd move line 62 above 61. That keeps the documented "FIRST match wins" engine contract (story.gd:66-71) untouched and preserves the flavour band lines for a first meeting. Optionally add an autotest assertion that no node lists a `band` variant before a `flag` variant whose flag any of that convo's own choices sets — as a NEW `_test_*` func at the end of autotest.gd plus one call at the marked hook, never an edit to an existing section.

title: Touch mode leaves the desktop ability bar's five variant glows on screen
claim: `set_touch_mode(true)` hides every desktop ability-slot widget except the `glow` TextureRect. `slot_boxes` entries carry a "glow" key (added with the variant-glow pass) but the hide list in `set_touch_mode` was never extended, so on the mobile/`--touch` build five soft radial glows stay painted across the bottom-centre of the screen with nothing behind them — and `update_stats` keeps re-tinting them every frame, so they are not even a static artefact.
evidence:
hud.gd:1001 builds the slot with the glow:
	slot_boxes.append({"border": border, "ring_style": ring_style, "bg": bg, "glow": glow, "icon": icon, "cd": cd, "num": num,
		"key": key, "cost": cost, "name": name_l, "was_ready": true, "flash_ms": 0})

hud.gd:4368-4371 hides everything but it:
	for box in slot_boxes:
		for k in ["border", "bg", "icon", "cd", "num", "key", "cost", "name"]:
			if box.get(k) != null:
				box[k].visible = not on

hud.gd:2400 keeps writing to it every frame regardless of touch mode:
			box["glow"].modulate = Color(0.42, 0.46, 0.6, 0.55)

The touch HUD mounts this path: touch_hud.gd:82 `game.hud.set_touch_mode(true)`.
repro: Launch with the touch HUD (mobile build, or `--touch` on desktop). touch_hud._ready() calls hud.set_touch_mode(true). Expected: the bottom desktop ability bar disappears entirely (its icons/cooldowns move to the right-hand arc). Actual: five 60x60 radial glow sprites remain at y=634, x from ~465 to ~745, tinted by each slot's equipped theme colour — visible over the world for the whole session, and they also sit under the mobile joystick/right-arc area.
fix: Add "glow" to the key list at hud.gd:4369 (`for k in ["border", "bg", "glow", "icon", "cd", "num", "key", "cost", "name"]:`). Better still, iterate the slot dict's Control values instead of a hand-maintained name list so a future widget can't be missed: `for k in box: var n: Control = box[k] as Control; if n != null: n.visible = not on` (typed local because `box[k]` is a Variant).

title: MP-20 ready check is dropped for good if the proposal lands while a menu is open
claim: `_on_proposal_changed` hides the ready-check card whenever any menu is open, and nothing re-renders it when the menu closes. `menus.close()` restores `game.hud.visible` but never re-drives the card, and `proposal_changed` does not fire again while the check is in flight — so a guest who happened to have the map/inventory/codex/pause screen open when `_rpc_propose` arrived never sees the Ready/Decline buttons, and the host's check dies on the 20 s timeout for the whole party.
evidence:
hud.gd:2652-2657:
	var data: Dictionary = sess.proposal_open
	if data.is_empty() or not game.net_online() \
			or (game.menus != null and game.menus.is_open()):
		_hide_ready_card()
		return
	_show_ready_card(sess, data)

menus.gd:69-98 `close()` restores the HUD but never touches the card:
	if game and game.hud:
		game.hud.visible = game.play_started

The only emitters are the session's own transitions (net_session.gd:2858, 2877, 2888, 2917, 2943) — none of them fire on a menu close, and net_session.gd:2826 `const CHECK_TIMEOUT := 20.0` closes the check without the guest ever answering.
repro: Co-op session, guest opens the Map (M) or Inventory (I). Host clears the chapter and presses the advance gate, which calls `propose_content("advance", …)` -> `_rpc_propose` on the guest -> `proposal_changed` emits while `menus.is_open()` is true -> `_hide_ready_card()`. Guest closes the map a second later: HUD comes back, no ready card, no way to answer. 20 s later every head gets "The ready check timed out." and the party does not advance.
fix: Re-drive the card when the overlay clears. Add a public `Hud.refresh_ready_card()` that just calls `_on_proposal_changed()`, and call it from `menus.close()` right after `game.hud.visible = game.play_started` (menus -> hud is a sibling call through `game`, so it obeys the derived->base rule). No tuning numbers involved.

title: Touch hit-test iterates buttons front-to-back, so the button drawn on top loses overlapping taps
claim: `_button_at`'s doc comment promises reverse iteration so the visually-topmost (last-added) button wins an overlap, but the loop walks `_btns.keys()` in insertion order — the same order `_make_button` adds the panels in, i.e. bottom-to-top. With the shipped BTN_LAYOUT the `interact` ("Act") and `potion_next` ("⟳") circles overlap by ~20 px; `interact` is drawn on top but `potion_next` is returned first, so a tap in that lens cycles the potion loadout instead of interacting.
repro: Mobile build, standing next to an NPC or a chest (so `game.interact_in_range` makes the Act button visible) with a multi-type potion loadout (so `potion_swap_useful()` makes ⟳ visible). Tap the part of the visible "Act" circle that lies within 40 px of (-238,-158) from the cluster origin. Expected: talk/open. Actual: the potion rotation cycles and the NPC is never engaged. The same inversion also mis-routes grabs in the layout editor, where `_button_at` picks which button a drag moves (touch_hud.gd:280).
fix: Walk the ids in reverse so the topmost-drawn button wins, matching the comment: `var ids: Array = _btns.keys(); for i in range(ids.size() - 1, -1, -1): var id: String = ids[i]` and keep the rest of the body. (Typed local because `ids[i]` is a Variant.) No layout constants need to change.

title: Cancelling the mail-delete confirmation dumps the player into the pause menu
claim: `open_confirm` falls back to `open_pause()` when the caller supplies no `on_cancel`, and the mailbox delete gate supplies none. Backing out of "Delete this letter?" therefore throws the player out of the mailbox and onto the system/pause screen instead of returning to the letter. The same omission is in journal.gd:401 (the BEGIN WEEKLY RUN gate). Sibling call sites that got it right — wardrobe.gd:238 passes `func() -> void: open(m)` — show the intended contract.
evidence:
mailbox.gd:134-136:
	else:
		m._btn(row, "  Delete letter  ", func() -> void:
			m.open_confirm("Delete this letter AND its unclaimed loot?", do_delete), Color(1.0, 0.65, 0.55))

menus.gd:599-604 is the fallback that fires:
	var no := func() -> void:
		if on_cancel.is_valid():
			close()
			on_cancel.call()
		else:
			open_pause()

ESC takes the same exit — menus.gd:5894-5896:
			elif current == "confirm" \
					or (current == "chapter_select" and chapter_replay):
				open_pause()  # back to the system menu, not out of it
repro: During play, click the HUD ✉ to open the mailbox, open a letter that still holds unclaimed loot, press "Delete letter", then press "Cancel" (or ESC). Expected: back to the letter with the loot intact. Actual: the "Paused — <chapter>" system menu opens; the mailbox is gone and the player has to navigate back to it.
fix: Pass the return path at the call site: `m.open_confirm("Delete this letter AND its unclaimed loot?", do_delete, func() -> void: open(m))` — matching wardrobe.gd:238. Do the same at journal.gd:401 (`func() -> void: open(m, "<tab>")`). Leave menus.gd's fallback alone so pause-menu callers keep their behaviour.

title: show_end_screen's title colour override is never restored, so later title cards wear it
claim: `show_end_screen` stamps a `font_color` theme override on the shared `title_label` and never clears it. `flash_title` — which reuses the same label for every location/chapter card — sets only text, position and alpha, so once a victory card has run, every subsequent title card renders in the victory gold instead of the built white. `boss_banner` does the identical stamp but explicitly restores it in its tween callback, which is the intended contract.
evidence:
hud.gd:696 builds the label white:
	title_label = _label(Vector2(0, 200), 44, Color(1, 1, 1), 1280, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER)

hud.gd:3673-3676 stamps and never restores:
func show_end_screen(text: String, sub: String, color: Color) -> void:
	overlay.color = Color(0, 0, 0, 0.75)
	title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)
	title_label.text = text

hud.gd:3586 + 3599 show the correct pattern for the same label:
	title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color(1.0, 0.32, 0.26))
	…
		title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color(1, 1, 1))

hud.gd:3609-3616 (`flash_title`) touches text/position/alpha only — no colour reset.
repro: Finish a chapter: game_flow.gd:2011 calls `hud.show_end_screen("VICTORY", vtext, Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.35))`. Dismiss the card (SPACE / click -> `game.victory_dismiss()`), which returns you to the live world rather than the title. Walk into the next room: game_world.gd:1017 calls `hud.flash_title(zones[i]["name"])`. Expected: the white location card. Actual: the room name renders in the victory gold, and stays gold for every card for the rest of the session.
fix: Reset the override at the top of `flash_title`: `title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color(1, 1, 1))` before setting the text (the same line `boss_banner` already uses at hud.gd:3599). The colour is presentation, not a tuning knob, so it stays in hud.gd.

title: Pounce tell tints are never reverted on the host, so a mob keeps a false "punish me" / "incoming pounce" colour forever
claim: The two pounce telegraph tints are written straight onto `sprite.modulate` and never restored to `base_mod`. Every other timed tell in the same file restores itself (counter at enemy.gd:1860, reflect at enemy.gd:1878, bite windup at enemy.gd:947), and the co-op GUEST mirror restores it on the `_net_tell` timer (enemy.gd:1439-1443). The HOST/solo path has no such restore, so a pouncer that overshoots stays dazed-yellow after its 1.1 s vulnerability window closes, and a pouncer that connects stays purple. The mob only returns to normal by accident, when the next hit-flash tween (enemy.gd:2481) or bite windup (enemy.gd:947) happens to overwrite it. Same class of miss, second site: enemy.gd:1659.
evidence:
enemy.gd:1847-1850

					pounce_whiff = Balance.MOB_POUNCE_WHIFF
					sprite.modulate = Color(1.6, 1.6, 0.5)  # dazed-yellow: punish me
		pounce_whiff = maxf(0.0, pounce_whiff - delta)

compare the sibling tells that DO revert -- enemy.gd:1857-1860
		if counter_t > 0.0:
			counter_t -= delta
			if counter_t <= 0.0:
				sprite.modulate = base_mod

and the guest mirror, which reverts on a timer -- enemy.gd:1440-1443
	if _net_tell_t > 0.0:
		_net_tell_t = maxf(0.0, _net_tell_t - delta)
		if _net_tell_t <= 0.0 and sprite != null:

second site, the crouch tint -- enemy.gd:1659-1660
			sprite.modulate = Color(1.8, 0.7, 2.0)       # purple crouch = incoming pounce
			_net_tell(Color(1.8, 0.7, 2.0), Balance.MOB_LUNGE_WINDUP + Balance.MOB_LUNGE_TIME)
repro: Solo (or as host). Stand ~200 px from a mob with the `pounce` trait so it leaps (Balance.MOB_LUNGE_RANGE), then sidestep so it overshoots by >96 px. It turns dazed-yellow and holds still for Balance.MOB_POUNCE_WHIFF (1.1 s). After 1.1 s it starts walking again -- and is STILL yellow. Do not hit it: it stays yellow indefinitely while chasing you, advertising a vulnerability window that has closed. Symmetric case: let a pounce CONNECT and the mob stays Color(1.8,0.7,2.0) purple ('incoming pounce') while it is not pouncing. In co-op the same mob on a guest's screen reverts correctly after MOB_LUNGE_WINDUP+MOB_LUNGE_TIME, so host and guest disagree about what the mob looks like.
fix: Give the pounce tells the same expiry-revert the counter/reflect tells already use, in `_tick_traits` (enemy.gd, the base layer that already owns `pounce_whiff` at enemy.gd:206 -- no new vars in a derived layer, no new tuning numbers: Balance.MOB_POUNCE_WHIFF / MOB_LUNGE_WINDUP / MOB_LUNGE_TIME already exist). Replace the bare decrement at enemy.gd:1850 with `if pounce_whiff > 0.0: pounce_whiff = maxf(0.0, pounce_whiff - delta); if pounce_whiff <= 0.0 and sprite != null: sprite.modulate = base_mod`, and add the matching `sprite.modulate = base_mod` on the else-branch of the enemy.gd:1847 overshoot test (a pounce that LANDED must drop the purple crouch too). Keep the guest path untouched -- it already matches.

title: chroma.gdshader discards the node's modulate entirely, so a chroma-skinned hero shows no rage tint and no alpha changes
claim: `fragment()` writes `COLOR` from the raw texture sample only -- it never reuses the incoming `COLOR` (which on canvas_item is modulate x TEXTURE, per the CLAUDE.md trap note) for either RGB or alpha, and it additionally hard-snaps alpha to 1.0 for any texel with a >= 0.5. The chroma material sits on `player.sprite` (skins.gd:395, applied from player_core.gd:850/861), which is the exact node player.gd re-assigns `modulate` on every frame for the berserk/rage body tint. Chromas are mutually exclusive with skins (player_core.gd:875), so the `_:` (base-class) arm of the rage match -- the one a chroma'd hero always takes -- is the arm whose colour is silently thrown away. Result: with a chroma equipped, Rage paints the aura ring but the BODY never changes colour, and any body alpha the game sets is ignored.
repro: Play a base warrior with no skin. Cast Rage and watch the body: it goes red (player.gd:446). Now equip any warrior chroma (Skins.CHROMAS['warrior'], e.g. 'crimson', skins.gd:30) and cast Rage again: the aura ring appears but the body colour does not change at all, because the shader overwrites COLOR with the palette-swapped texture. Same for any alpha the game puts on the body while a chroma is live -- the `col.a >= 0.5 ? 1.0` branch also forces those texels opaque.
fix: Two seams, both inside the shader + its one CPU writer. (1) Restore the modulate alpha the way silhouette.gdshader does, recovering it from the premultiplied input rather than the texture: `float mod_a = col.a > 0.001 ? COLOR.a / col.a : 0.0;` and emit `out_a * mod_a` instead of `out_a`. (2) Add a `uniform vec3 body_tint = vec3(1.0);` multiplied into `result` and `col.rgb`, and push the rage/flash colour into it instead of into `modulate` whenever a chroma material is live -- via a small setter on `player_core.gd` (where `chroma` and `sprite` already live, so the call flows player.gd -> player_core.gd, derived->base) called from the same block at player.gd:437-448. The tint colours stay where they are today (player.gd's per-skin match, a content table, not a tuning knob); no new numbers land outside balance.gd.

title: sfx() cutoff tween fades and re-stamps a pooled AudioStreamPlayer that has already been recycled for a different sound
claim: `sfx(..., cutoff)` schedules a 2.5 s-delayed volume ramp on the pool player it happened to pick, but the pool is a first-free round-robin (game_base.gd:3024-3028) and every recorded boss roar is far shorter than the 2.5 s cutoff, so that slot is handed to another sound long before the tween fires. The `chosen.stream == this_stream` guard covers only `stop()`; the `tween_property(chosen, "volume_db", -40.0, 0.4)` and the unconditional `chosen.volume_db = -8.0` both hit whatever is playing on the slot at that moment. Measured durations of the shipped roars: roar_stormwarden.wav 1.30 s, roar_nullwarden.wav 1.40 s, roar_vargoth.wav 1.64 s, roar_choirmother.wav 1.70 s -- all under the 2.5 s in the only cutoff call site (boss.gd:228). The synthesized fallback `roar` is shorter still (Sfx.tone(95, 38, 0.75, ...), sfx.gd:550). Two audible effects: a random SFX fades to silence for ~0.4 s about 2.5 s after every boss roar, and any `vol_db` offset on the sound occupying that slot is reset to the -8 dB default mid-play.
evidence:
game_base.gd:3036-3045
	if cutoff > 0.0:
		var this_stream: AudioStream = chosen.stream
		var tween := create_tween()
		tween.tween_interval(cutoff)
		tween.tween_property(chosen, "volume_db", -40.0, 0.4)
		tween.tween_callback(func() -> void:
			if chosen.stream == this_stream:
				chosen.stop()
			chosen.volume_db = -8.0
		)

the pool is recycled as soon as a player stops -- game_base.gd:3024-3028
	var chosen: AudioStreamPlayer = sound_pool[0]
	for sp in sound_pool:
		if not sp.playing:
			chosen = sp
			break

the only cutoff caller -- boss.gd:226-228
	var key := "roar_" + kind
	# Long recordings (the real wolf howl) get faded after ~2.5s.
	game.sfx(key if game.sounds.has(key) else "roar", 1.0, 2.5)
repro: Fight Vargoth (roar_vargoth.wav, 1.64 s). Boss.roar() picks a free pool slot and schedules the cutoff at t=2.5 s. The roar ends at t=1.64 s, the slot goes idle, and the next sfx() -- a sword swing, an ehit, a footstep -- takes that same slot. At t=2.5..2.9 s that in-flight sound is tweened down to -40 dB and then slammed back to -8 dB: a hit or cast audibly drops out for ~0.4 s, every roar, and any sound started in that window with a vol_db offset (e.g. `sfx("step_1", 1.0, 0.0, -8.0)` from tick_footsteps, game_base.gd:2851) loses its offset. Deterministic under a headless log by stamping the pool index.
fix: Make the cutoff bind to the PLAY, not the slot. Stamp a monotonically increasing id on the player before `play()` (`chosen.set_meta("play_id", _sfx_play_id)`), capture it, and have both the fade and the callback no-op unless the meta still matches -- and restore the volume to the level THIS play set (`-8.0 + vol_db`), not a hard-coded -8.0. Alternatively reserve one dedicated long-form player outside `sound_pool` for cutoff plays. The 2.5 s cutoff and the -8/-40 dB levels are tuning numbers and belong in balance.gd rather than inline in game_base.gd:3033/3040/3044 and boss.gd:228.
